.engramdb/memories/staging-export-bucket-points-at-the-prod-bucket_01a0f827-a9be-7630-bc3c-d41497fa4ba3.md:15:In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Never run scripts/export.py against staging without `--dry-run`.

Yes, but only with `--dry-run`:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

A project memory records that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. A real run against staging would write to prod data. The script has a `--dry-run` flag, and `--env` accepts `staging`. I haven't run anything.

Two caveats:
- The script only prints the target bucket (`exporting staging to <bucket> (dry_run=True)`). I only read the first lines of it, so I haven't confirmed that `--dry-run` skips every write. Skim the rest of the script before you trust it.
- The dry run's printed bucket should show the prod bucket if the memory is right, so it also doubles as a check on the hazard.

If you want a real (non-dry) test run, point `EXPORT_BUCKET` at a non-prod bucket first, or use `--env dev`, whose default bucket is `ledgerline-exports-dev`.

I can run the dry run for you if you want, but it needs staging credentials in the environment.
